steps.title: Import required Node.js modules
steps.instruction: Import the required Node.js modules: fs/promises for file operations, path for path manipulation, http for creating the server, and sharp for image processing.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the modules. Remember to use the correct module names: 'fs/promises', 'path', 'http', and 'sharp'.
steps.seedCode: // Import the required Node.js modules here
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have import statements for fs/promises, path, http, and sharp modules.
successCriteria: All four modules (fs/promises, path, http, and sharp) are imported using the import statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported all the required Node.js modules needed for image processing and HTTP server functionality.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some modules, but not all. Make sure to import fs/promises, path, http, and sharp.
steps.feedbackWrong: The required modules are not imported. You need to import fs/promises, path, http, and sharp for this lesson.

steps.title: Create the HTTP server
steps.instruction: Create an HTTP server using the imported http module and configure it to listen on port 3000.
steps.hint: Use the http.createServer() method and call .listen() on the returned server object.
steps.expectedOutcome: A server is created and configured to listen on port 3000.
successCriteria: The server is created with http.createServer() and configured to listen on port 3000.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created an HTTP server that will listen on port 3000.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using http.createServer() and calling .listen(3000) on the server object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server wasn't properly created. Remember to use http.createServer() and configure it to listen on port 3000.

steps.title: Define the request handler function
steps.instruction: Define an async function named 'requestHandler' that takes 'req' and 'res' parameters and will handle all incoming HTTP requests to the server.
steps.hint: Create an async function that accepts the request and response objects as parameters. The function body can be empty for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have an async function named 'requestHandler' that accepts 'req' and 'res' parameters.
successCriteria: An async function named 'requestHandler' is defined with 'req' and 'res' parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the request handler function. This function will process all incoming HTTP requests.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function is async, named 'requestHandler', and accepts both 'req' and 'res' parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function definition doesn't match requirements. Check that it's async, named 'requestHandler', and has both 'req' and 'res' parameters.

steps.title: Parse URL parameters from the request
steps.instruction: Inside your request handler function, parse the request URL to extract width and height parameters from the query string.
steps.hint: Use the built-in URL object to parse the request URL and access its searchParams property to get query parameters.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your request handler will be able to extract width and height values from the query string of incoming requests.
successCriteria: The request handler function uses the URL object to parse the request URL and extracts width and height parameters from searchParams.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully parsed the URL parameters. The width and height values are now accessible in your handler.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the URL object correctly and extracting both width and height parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using the URL constructor with the request URL and accessing searchParams.get() for both parameters.

steps.title: Validate input parameters
steps.instruction: Inside the requestHandler function, add validation logic to check that the width and height parameters are valid positive numbers. If either is invalid, send a 400 status with an error message and return early.
steps.hint: Parse the width and height from the URL parameters, then check if they are numbers greater than 0. Use res.writeHead and res.end to send an error response if validation fails.
steps.expectedOutcome: The request handler will now validate width and height parameters before proceeding, returning a 400 error for invalid inputs.
successCriteria: The validation logic checks that width and height are positive numbers, sends a 400 status with an error message if invalid, and returns early.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added input validation to ensure only valid image dimensions are processed.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some validation, but make sure to check both width and height are positive numbers and send a proper 400 error response.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation logic is missing or incorrect. Ensure you parse width and height, validate them as positive numbers, and handle invalid cases with a 400 response.

steps.title: Read the source image file
steps.instruction: Inside your requestHandler function, use fs.promises.readFile to read the source image file 'input.jpg' from the filesystem. Store the result in a variable named imageBuffer.
steps.hint: You'll need to use await with readFile since it returns a promise. Make sure your function is async to use await.
steps.expectedOutcome: The requestHandler function will now be able to read the image file asynchronously and store its binary data in imageBuffer.
successCriteria: The requestHandler function uses fs.promises.readFile to read 'input.jpg' and stores the result in imageBuffer.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented file reading. The imageBuffer variable now contains the binary data of the source image, ready for processing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using fs.promises.readFile (not fs.readFileSync) and storing the result in a variable named imageBuffer.
steps.feedbackWrong: The code doesn't properly read the image file. Remember to use fs.promises.readFile with await inside your async requestHandler function.

steps.title: Resize the image using Sharp
steps.instruction: Inside the requestHandler function, after reading the source image file, use the Sharp library to resize the image to the specified width and height.
steps.hint: Use the sharp() function with the image data, then chain .resize() with the width and height parameters.
steps.expectedOutcome: The image data will be resized to the specified dimensions using the Sharp library.
successCriteria: Sharp is used to resize the image with the width and height parameters from the URL.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully integrated Sharp to resize the image based on the URL parameters.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the sharp() function with the image data and chaining .resize() with the width and height parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The image resizing step is missing or incorrect. Remember to use the Sharp library to resize the image to the specified width and height.

steps.title: Send the resized image as response
steps.instruction: Inside the requestHandler function, after the image resizing logic, set the Content-Type header to 'image/jpeg' and send the resized image buffer as the response body.
steps.hint: Use res.setHeader() to set the Content-Type header and res.end() to send the buffer.
steps.expectedOutcome: The request handler will now properly send the resized image as an HTTP response with correct headers.
successCriteria: The Content-Type header is set to 'image/jpeg' and the resized image buffer is sent as the response body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully set up the response to send the resized image with proper headers.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're setting the Content-Type header and sending the buffer in the response.
steps.feedbackWrong: The response isn't properly configured. Check that you're setting the Content-Type header and sending the image buffer.

steps.title: Add error handling for invalid requests
steps.instruction: Wrap the existing request handler logic in a try-catch block to handle errors for missing files, invalid parameters, and processing errors.
steps.hint: Add try { ... } catch (error) { ... } around the existing logic inside your requestHandler function. In the catch block, send appropriate HTTP error responses.
steps.expectedOutcome: The request handler will now gracefully handle errors by sending appropriate HTTP error responses instead of crashing.
successCriteria: The requestHandler function contains a try-catch block that wraps the main logic and sends HTTP error responses in the catch block.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added error handling to make your endpoint more robust.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some error handling, but make sure to wrap all the main logic in the try block and send proper HTTP responses in the catch block.
steps.feedbackWrong: The error handling isn't implemented correctly. Review how to use try-catch blocks and HTTP error responses in Node.js.

steps.title: Test the endpoint with a sample request
steps.instruction: Start the server by calling server.listen() on port 3000 and add a console.log to confirm it's running.
steps.hint: Call the listen method on your server object with port 3000 and a callback function that logs a message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will start and log a confirmation message, making the endpoint ready for testing.
successCriteria: The server is started on port 3000 with a console.log message confirming it's running.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Your server is now running and ready to accept requests. You can test it by visiting http://localhost:3000?width=300&height=200 in your browser or using a tool like curl.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the server, but make sure you included a console.log message to confirm it's running. Check that you're listening on port 3000.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't properly started. You need to call server.listen() with port 3000 and a callback function that logs a message.
